finops_results.policy_name: S3 - consider deleting incomplete multi-part uploads
finops_results.policy_message: When S3 uploads fail, the incomplete multi-part data still lives in S3 and costs money even though it's not a usable S3 object. You can avoid paying for that by setting the number of days after which these are deleted. We suggest 7 days.

issues.description: Add a lifecycle rule which specifies a configuration to abort incomplete multipart uploads

finops_results.policy_name: S3 - consider deleting or moving non-current object versions to a cheaper storage class
finops_results.policy_message: S3 can store multiple versions of the same object. However, most of the time, you only need the current version. So you could set the number of days after which non-current objects are deleted. Ensure that you do not need non-current object versions first.

finops_results.policy_name: [EC2.9, EC2.25] Amazon EC2 and launch templates should not associate a public IPv4 address
finops_results.policy_message: EC2 instances and launch templates should not have a public IPv4 address to reduce attack surface and prevent direct internet exposure. Use NAT gateways for outbound connectivity and AWS Systems Manager Session Manager for secure instance access. Corresponds to AWS Security Hub control EC2.9 and EC2.25.

issues.description: Consider disabling `associate_public_ip_address`. Set it to `false` and use NAT gateways for outbound connectivity.

finops_results.policy_name: EC2 - require Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2)
finops_results.policy_message: Consider using IMDSv2 for EC2 instances to provide enhanced security protections against multiple vulnerability classes. Corresponds to AWS Security Hub control EC2.8.

finops_results.policy_name: S3 - consider using Intelligent-Tiering or adding a lifecycle policy
finops_results.policy_message: Use a lifecycle policy to reduce object storage costs. You can reduce storage costs by defining policies that remove or move objects to a less expensive S3 storage class. For example, a bucket storing 1TB of data in a standard storage class would have a monthly cost of $23. If the same data was moved to Glacier Flexible Retrieval storage class it would have a monthly cost of just $3.60. That's a 84% cost saving.

issues.description: Add a lifecycle rule which specifies a transition or expiration configuration

finops_results.policy_name: EBS - consider upgrading gp2 volumes to gp3
finops_results.policy_message: gp3 volumes are the latest generation of general-purpose SSD-based EBS volumes that enable you to provision performance independent of storage capacity, while providing up to **20% lower price per GB** than existing gp2 volumes. With gp3 volumes, you can scale IOPS (input/output operations per second) and throughput without needing to provision additional block storage capacity. This means you only pay for the storage you need.

finops_results.policy_name: EBS - consider updating io1/io2 volumes to gp3
finops_results.policy_message: io1 and io2 volume types that need less than 16K IOPS, and less than 1000 MB/s Throughput, and don’t use Multi-Attach should be switched to gp3 as that is **at least 2X cheaper**. For example, a gp3 volume with 16TB storage, 16K IOPS and 1000 MB/s Throughput costs $1.4K/month vs $3K/month on io1 or io2.

finops_results.policy_name: [S3.5] S3 buckets should require requests to use SSL
finops_results.policy_message: S3 buckets should have a bucket policy that denies non-SSL (HTTP) requests. Without this policy, data in transit is not protected from interception. Add a bucket policy with a Deny statement for requests where aws:SecureTransport is false.

issues.description: Attach a bucket policy with a `Deny` statement for requests where `aws:SecureTransport` is `false`, so non-SSL requests are rejected.

finops_results.policy_message: Graviton instances are around 20% cheaper than equivalent x86 instances.

finops_results.policy_name: EC2 - consider using latest generation instances for t family instances
finops_results.policy_message: Upgrade to Amazon EC2 t3 instances for improved Intel Xeon Processors, AWS Nitro System and EBS optimization by default, all at lower price point than previous generations. For example a `t2.medium` instance with 4 GiB of memory and 2 vCPUs (for a 4h 48m burst) has a monthly cost of $33. Whereas a `t3.medium` instance with equivalent machine specs costs just $30. That's a 10% cost saving for a more performant machine.

finops_results.policy_name: Storage Account - consider disabling public network access
finops_results.policy_message: Storage accounts should disable public network access to prevent direct internet exposure and improve security posture. Restrict access to private endpoints and virtual networks only.

issues.description: Set `public_network_access_enabled` to `false` to prevent direct internet exposure and improve security posture.

finops_results.policy_name: Storage Accounts - consider using a lifecycle policy for blob storage
finops_results.policy_message: A lifecycle policy should be defined for Azure blob storage accounts to automate the transition of your data based on its usage pattern to optimize storage costs, improve performance, or to delete blobs that are no longer needed.

issues.description: Set `blob_properties[0].last_access_time_enabled` to `true` to take advantage of access time tracking
Attach a storage management policy to this storage account to take advantage of lifecycle policies

finops_results.policy_name: Storage Accounts - consider upgrading account kind to StorageV2
finops_results.policy_message: Azure recommends general-purpose v2 accounts for most storage scenarios. v2 accounts incorporate all of the functionality of general-purpose v1 and Blob storage accounts, and have the latest features such as lifecycle management and access tiers.

finops_results.policy_name: Compute - consider using current generation machine types
finops_results.policy_message:
N1s are first-generation general purpose VMs. For most use-cases (excluding GPU workloads), Google recommends one of their second-generation types such as:

- **E2** offers the lowest total cost of ownership with up to 31% savings compared to N1.
- **N2** uses 2nd Gen Intel Xeon Scalable Processors (Cascade Lake) and offers a greater than 20% price-performance improvement for many workloads and support up to 25% more memory per vCPU.
- **N2D** uses latest 2nd Gen AMD EPYC (Rome) CPUs, and support the highest core count and memory of any general-purpose Compute Engine VM.

finops_results.policy_name: Cloud Storage - consider deleting incomplete multipart uploads
finops_results.policy_message: When Cloud Storage uploads fail, the incomplete multipart data still lives in the bucket and costs money even though it's not a usable object. Add a lifecycle rule to abort incomplete multipart uploads after a set number of days (suggest 7 days).

issues.description: Add a lifecycle rule with an `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` action to clean up incomplete uploads

finops_results.policy_name: Cloud Storage - consider deleting non-current object versions
finops_results.policy_message: Cloud Storage can store multiple versions of the same object when versioning is enabled. Use lifecycle rules to automatically delete non-current versions based on age or version count to reduce storage costs.

finops_results.policy_name: Cloud Storage - consider adding lifecycle rules to transition or expire objects
finops_results.policy_message: Use lifecycle rules to reduce object storage costs. You can define rules that delete objects or move them to a cheaper storage class based on age or other conditions.

issues.description: Add a lifecycle rule with a `SetStorageClass` or `Delete` action to define object lifecycle transitions
